Repo: LectorIA-meta, branch `contracts-reader`, worktree root is the workspace. Read AGENTS.md and SECURITY.md first; they are binding (core purity, server-only, generic client errors, design palette from app/tokens.css, never purple, desktop only, writing rules).

Owner goal: music generation must not block development. Define clean contracts and module boundaries across the system so any module can be swapped. For now it is enough that the reader requests a track for a scene, gets one, and starts playing it. Real MusicGen tracks are iterated in parallel and must drop in later by replacing a manifest and audio files only, with no code change.

Skills to apply (read the files in `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`; several are user-invocable-only, so read them directly): architect, principle-foundational-thinking, principle-type-system-discipline, typescript-best-practices, ponytail (full, in AGENTS.md), ponytail-review, principle-prove-it-works, unslop, technical-writing.

## Scope

1. `docs/contracts.md` (short, unslopped, sentence-case headings, under 5000 tokens). Each module: inputs, outputs, owner side (core, server, app client, pipeline, static assets). At minimum:
   - BookData: book.json, scenes.json, analysis.json, shapes already in core/types.ts. Name which fields the reader consumes.
   - MusicLibrary manifest (shape below) and where it lives.
   - Track selection (pure core function).
   - Player (client module: input is a track or null; owns audio elements, crossfade, loop, play/pause, volume).
   - Image API, contract only: request `{ bookId, textVersion, firstN, lastN }` (paragraph ordinals of the selection), response `{ url }` (a Vercel Blob URL) or a generic error. Cache key = paragraph range of the selection's touched paragraphs + textVersion + promptVersion, deterministic Blob path, `head()` before generate, never return bytes. Same paragraph reuses the image.
   - Chat API, contract only: request `{ bookId, textVersion, positionN, spoilerMode, messages }`, streamed text response. Server builds context from the book text up to positionN (whole book when spoilerMode), book prefix first and question last for prompt caching, answers only from that text.
   - Quotas and budget boundary: server-only, integer micro-dollars, Redis INCRBY reserve before each model call, DECRBY refund; clients never see keys or raw errors.
   Types for all of this live in `core/` (pure: no env, no fs, no fetch, no node imports, no server-only). `server/` and `app/` depend only on core types. Image and chat get typed request/response types and nothing else now: no routes, no implementations.

2. Music contract in core (new file, e.g. `core/music.ts`, tests beside it):
   - `MusicManifest = { version: number; tracks: Track[] }`, `Track = { id: string; src: string; label: string; vector: Vector8; intensity: number; tempo: number; durationSec: number; loop: boolean }`. Reuse `Vector8`, `EMOTIONS`, `FEATURE_WEIGHTS` and `buildFeatures` from core/types.ts and core/cluster.ts rather than duplicating (move `buildFeatures` only if importing cluster.ts into client code would drag in something unsuitable; it should not).
   - A small pure `parseManifest(json: unknown): MusicManifest` validator (throws on bad shape: unknown version, missing fields, vector not over the 8 ids, numbers out of 0..1, src not a relative `/music/` path or https URL). The client calls it on the fetched manifest so a bad drop-in fails loudly in dev.
   - `selectTrack(scene: { vector: Vector8; intensity: number; tempo: number } | null, manifest, currentTrackId?: string | null, opts?: { margin?: number; exclude?: string[] }): Track | null`: cosine similarity over `buildFeatures` (vector plus weighted intensity and tempo). Hysteresis: keep the current track unless the best candidate beats it by `margin` (default 0.05, one-line why). A null scene (hard failure, no vector) keeps the current track; with no current track it returns null. Empty manifest returns null. Ties break by manifest order, deterministic.
   - `nextAlternative(scene, manifest, currentTrackId)`: the next best track by similarity after the current one, wrapping around, so repeated presses cycle through every track. Returns the current track when the manifest has one track.
   - Product rule: a skip overrides until the next scene. The reader keeps the override per scene; when the active scene changes, selection runs again from the override track as current.

3. Placeholder manifest. Pick the simpler option and say why in docs/contracts.md: a static `public/music/manifest.json` fetched by the client is the expected choice (no route, served from CDN, swap = replace files). Add `public/music/README.md`: how to swap in real tracks (replace manifest.json and files, keep the shape, bump version), and the CC-BY-NC note for MusicGen output (non-commercial hackathon demo). A test loads the committed manifest through `parseManifest` and checks every src file exists under public/.

4. Reader (app/). Desktop layout: the book centered at the reading measure, a quiet companion side panel slot (keep "Chat comes later." style placeholder, no chat code), and a compact player bar.
   - A server component (app/page.tsx) reads data/books/oz/book.json, scenes.json and analysis.json at build time (static import or fs in a server-only loader under server/) and builds a compact reader model with a pure core function, e.g. `buildReaderModel(book, analysis)` → `{ bookId, textVersion, title, author, chapters: [{ ch, title, scenes: [{ id, title, emotion: {vector,intensity,tempo} | null, paragraphs: [{ id, n, text }] }] }] }` in reading order. Do not ship analysis internals (jev, muse_override, provenance) to the client. Validate ordering in the core function (scenes in n order, covering paragraphs) and test it.
   - Continuous scroll, no pagination. Chapter headings, then paragraphs grouped by scene (a `section` per scene with `data-scene-id`, paragraph ids like `c12p34` from the existing ids helper). No visible scene chrome beyond maybe a subtle divider.
   - A client component tracks the active scene with IntersectionObserver: the scene whose section crosses a reading line near the top third of the viewport. Keep it simple and correct when scrolling fast or jumping.
   - Player module (client, e.g. `app/player/`): takes the selected track; two `audio` elements with a crossfade on change (about 1.5 s; 0 when prefers-reduced-motion), loop, play/pause button (audio starts only after the user presses play, respecting autoplay rules), volume slider, a "Change track" button that calls nextAlternative and holds that override until the scene changes. Shows the current track label and the active scene title, small and quiet. Accessible: real buttons, aria-labels, visible focus, keyboard usable.
   - Fetch the manifest client-side from `/music/manifest.json` once, parse with `parseManifest`; on failure the reader still works without music and the bar shows a short neutral message.
   - Style with existing tokens in app/tokens.css; extend tokens only if needed. Meta blue `#0866FF` single accent, no purple, no gradients, no glassmorphism, no emoji icons. Motion under 200 ms for UI (the audio crossfade is not UI motion). Desktop only.
   - Keep the CSP working: audio from 'self' is allowed by `media-src 'self' blob:`; manifest fetch is `connect-src 'self'`. Do not loosen the CSP.

5. Tests (vitest, beside the code): selectTrack (nearest by cosine, hysteresis keeps current within margin and switches beyond it, null scene keeps current, empty manifest, exclude, deterministic ties), nextAlternative (cycles all tracks, single track), parseManifest (good, bad shapes), buildReaderModel (reading order, scene ordering by n, every paragraph exactly once, null emotion for failed scenes, no analysis internals), committed manifest test. Do not add a DOM testing library; player and observer logic that can be pure should be pure and tested, the rest is checked by `next build` and a manual run.

- Every authored file under 5000 tokens (the pre-commit hook enforces it). public/ and data/books/ are already exempt.

3|# Ponytail
4|
5|You are a lazy senior developer. The best code is the code never written. You solve the whole problem with the least new code. End your reply with one or two lines: what you skipped or did not check, and any risk the user must know.
6|
7|Active for the whole session until the user says "stop ponytail" or "normal mode". Switch level: `/ponytail lite|full|ultra`.

9|## Before you write
10|
11|Read the task and the code it touches. List every place your change must reach: callers, tests, fixtures, config, exports. Check what your change could break for users: data it would destroy or expose, callers that stop working. That is scope. Extra features are not.
12|
13|## The smallest complete change
14|
15|Take the first option that fully works:
16|
17|1. Does it need to exist? Skip features, options and flexibility nobody asked for, and name them in one line. A vague request ("build me X") gets the smallest version that does the core job.
18|2. Already in this codebase (a helper, component, service, pattern)? Use it the way the surrounding code does.
19|3. Standard library or a platform feature? Use it, unless the project has its own. A house component beats a native widget.
20|4. An installed dependency? Use it. Never add a dependency for a few lines.
21|5. Can it be one line a reader gets at a glance? One line.
22|6. Otherwise: the minimum code that works.
23|
24|- Be lazy about the solution, never about the change itself: finish every part the task needs, including the callers, tests and fixtures your change breaks.
25|- No abstraction, wrapper, type conversion, option, config, boilerplate or "for later" code nobody asked for. Keep values in the form the platform already gives you. Deletion beats addition. Keep the structure the codebase already has: its layers, interfaces and conventions.
26|- The shortest working diff wins, once you know everything it must touch. A one-liner that needs decoding is not short.
27|- Comment only the why the code cannot show, in one line.
28|- Bug fix: before you edit, grep every caller of the function you touch, then fix the root cause once in the shared code.
29|- Code you move or merge keeps its error handling and validation.
30|- Between options of equal size, take the one that is correct on edge cases.
31|- Lazy code without its check is unfinished: new non-trivial logic (a branch, a loop, a parser, money or security, or a whole new script or app) leaves one small test or an assert-based self-check. Trivial changes need none.
32|- A shortcut with a known limit gets a code comment in this form: `shortcut: <the limit>, <when to upgrade>`.
33|

79|- Public-domain books only.

84|## Product rules
85|
86|Owner decisions. Short and binding.
87|
88|- Desktop first. No mobile or iOS work now.
89|- The reader uses continuous scroll. The unit is the scene.
90|- A chapter holds several scenes. Each scene has its own emotion. Music changes at scene boundaries inside a chapter. No pagination.
91|- Reading position is the first paragraph visible at the top, tracked with IntersectionObserver.
92|- Paragraph ids carry a global ordinal `n`. Compare `n`, never id strings.
93|- `book.json` is frozen with a `textVersion` hash. Every cache key includes it.
94|- Scenes cover each chapter's paragraphs with no gaps and no overlaps. No scene crosses a chapter boundary.
95|- Emotions are distributions. Each scene stores the full Jev probability vector over the 8 ids, plus `intensity` (0 to 1) and `tempo` (energy, 0 to 1). The Muse override on low confidence edits the vector and records that it did. It never swaps in a single label.
96|- Music is about 15 tracks, pre-generated offline with MusicGen on Modal as one coherent soundtrack: same orchestra and instrumentation, same leitmotif style. Each track is a weighted blend of emotions and carries an emotion vector plus intensity and tempo. The proposed way to pick the blends: cluster the Oz scene vectors and use the centroids as track prompts.
97|- The player picks the track nearest to the scene vector, by cosine similarity over the vector plus intensity and tempo. Hysteresis stops it from flipping on small changes. Skip or change track overrides until the next scene.
98|- The owner listens to short clips before any full generation. Agents do not run Modal until the owner says so.
99|- MusicGen weights are CC-BY-NC. The hackathon demo is non-commercial. The generated tracks must say so in their README.
100|- Chat is low priority and simple. The context is the book text up to the reader's current position. The book prefix goes first and the question goes last, so readers share the prompt cache. Oz is about 55k tokens.
101|- The chat system prompt answers only from the provided text. It refuses knowledge beyond it, even if the model knows the book.

1|# Design: task 5 contracts and scene reader
2|
3|Goal: define module contracts so music generation never blocks the reader, then build the scene reader with two placeholder tracks. Real tracks drop in later by replacing files only. Branch `contracts-reader`. Binding inputs: AGENTS.md, SECURITY.md, `core/types.ts`, `core/cluster.ts`, `next.config.ts`, `data/books/oz/music-clusters.json`. This step writes only this doc. The implementer writes `docs/contracts.md`, `core/music.ts`, the manifest, the reader, and the tests.
4|
5|## Module layout
6|
7|```text
8|core/
9|  types.ts    existing book, scene, emotion shapes plus new contract types
10|  music.ts    MusicManifest, Track, parseManifest, selectTrack, nextAlternative
11|  reader.ts   ReaderModel, buildReaderModel
12|  cluster.ts  unchanged, lends buildFeatures to music.ts
13|server/
14|  books.ts    server-only loader: reads oz json, returns Book plus scenes
15|app/
16|  page.tsx    server component: loads data, builds model, renders text
17|  reader.tsx  client container: observer, selection, override, manifest fetch
18|  player/     client player: audio elements, controls, crossfade
19|  tokens.css  unchanged unless a player style needs a token
20|public/music/
21|  manifest.json   placeholder manifest, version 1
22|  README.md       swap guide plus CC-BY-NC note
23|  placeholder/    two mp3 clips, already present
24|```
25|
26|Ownership: `core` is pure and owns every shared type plus selection and model building. `server` owns file reads and env. `app` owns rendering and playback. Import direction is `core <- server` and `core <- app`. Neither `server` nor client components import each other. `app/page.tsx` may import `server/books.ts`. Client files never do.
27|
28|## Core types and signatures
29|
30|New file `core/music.ts`. It reuses `Vector8`, `EMOTIONS`, `FEATURE_WEIGHTS`, and `buildFeatures` from `core/types.ts` and `core/cluster.ts`. Choice: reuse `buildFeatures` in place because `cluster.ts` imports only types, so client code gains no Node or heavy code.
31|
32|```ts
33|export interface Track {
34|  id: string; src: string; label: string;
35|  vector: Vector8; intensity: number; tempo: number;
36|  durationSec: number; loop: boolean;
37|}
38|export interface MusicManifest { version: number; tracks: Track[]; }
39|export function parseManifest(json: unknown): MusicManifest;
40|export function selectTrack(
41|  scene: { vector: Vector8; intensity: number; tempo: number } | null,
42|  manifest: MusicManifest,
43|  currentTrackId?: string | null,
44|  opts?: { margin?: number; exclude?: string[] },
45|): Track | null;
46|export function nextAlternative(
47|  scene: { vector: Vector8; intensity: number; tempo: number } | null,
48|  manifest: MusicManifest,
49|  currentTrackId: string | null,
50|): Track | null;
51|```
52|
53|Rules from the spec: `parseManifest` throws on unknown version, missing fields, a vector not over the 8 ids, numbers outside 0..1, or a `src` that is not a `/music/` relative path or https URL. `selectTrack` scores cosine similarity over `buildFeatures` output, keeps the current track unless the best beats it by `margin` (default 0.05), returns null for a null scene with no current track, returns null for an empty manifest, and breaks ties by manifest order. `nextAlternative` ranks by similarity after the current track and wraps around, so repeats cycle all tracks; one track returns itself. 54|
55|Contract-only types live in `core/types.ts`, with no routes and no implementations:
56|
57|```ts
58|export interface ImageRequest { bookId: string; textVersion: string; firstN: number; lastN: number; }
59|export interface ImageResponse { url: string; }
60|export interface ChatRequest { bookId: string; textVersion: string; positionN: number; spoilerMode: boolean; messages: { role: "user" | "assistant"; text: string }[]; }

62|
63|Quota and budget stay server-only: integer micro-dollars, Redis `INCRBY` reserve before each model call, `DECRBY` refund after. Clients never see keys or raw errors. 66|
67|New pure function in `core/reader.ts`:
68|
69|```ts
70|export interface ReaderParagraph { id: string; n: number; text: string; }
71|export interface ReaderScene {
72|  id: string; title: string;
73|  emotion: { vector: Vector8; intensity: number; tempo: number } | null;
74|  paragraphs: ReaderParagraph[];
75|}

78|  bookId: string; textVersion: string; title: string; author: string;

83|  analysis: { scenes: AnalyzedScene[] },
84|): ReaderModel;

86|
87|It joins paragraphs to scenes by `n` ranges in reading order, keeps `final` emotion or null for failed scenes, and drops analysis internals (`jev`, `muse_override`, provenance) so they never reach the client. 88|
89|## Server side
90|
91|`server/books.ts` starts with `import 'server-only'` and exposes one function:
92|
93|```ts
94|export function loadOzBook(): { book: Book; scenes: AnalyzedScene[] };
95|```
96|
97|It reads `data/books/oz/book.json`, `scenes.json`, and `analysis.json` with a static import (build time, no request cost) and returns typed values. `app/page.tsx` calls it, runs `buildReaderModel`, and renders chapters, scene sections, and paragraphs as server HTML. 98|

100|
101|`app/page.tsx` owns layout: centered book column at the reading measure, quiet side panel with the "Chat comes later." placeholder, and the player bar slot. No chat code. Scene sections carry `data-scene-id` with a subtle divider and no other chrome.
102|
103|`app/reader.tsx` is the client container. It owns the manifest fetch (once, from `/music/manifest.json`, parsed with `parseManifest`), the active scene id, the current track id, and the skip override. On manifest failure the reader still renders and the bar shows a short neutral message. It passes the chosen track to the player.
104|
105|`app/player/` owns only playback: audio elements, play state, volume, and the skip button wired through an `onSkip` prop from the container.
106|
107|## Active scene tracking
108|
109|One `IntersectionObserver` watches scene sections. The reading line sits near the top third of the viewport, set with a `rootMargin` band around minus 30 percent. The active scene is the intersecting section whose top edge is nearest above the line. Choice: observer with a band instead of scroll math because jumps and fast scrolls then resolve in one callback with no position cache to maintain. Edge handling: short scenes still cross the band since sections span their paragraphs; when nothing intersects (fast fling between frames), keep the last active scene rather than guessing. On mount, compute from current scroll position so reloads mid book start on the right scene.
110|
111|## Player state machine
112|
113|States: `idle`, `playing`, `paused`, `crossfading`, `no music`. `idle` means no user gesture yet; `no music` means the manifest failed or is empty.
114|
115|```text
116|idle --press play--> playing (or crossfading when a track is already selected)
117|playing --track change--> crossfading --1.5s--> playing
118|playing --press pause--> paused --press play--> playing
119|any --manifest failure or empty--> no music
120|```
121|
122|Two `audio` elements fade against each other on change over about 1.5 s, then the old one pauses. `prefers-reduced-motion` sets the fade to 0. Choice: plain audio elements with a volume ramp instead of Web Audio because nothing here needs decoding or filtering, and native elements keep codec and loop behavior free. Loop is on. Audio starts only after the user presses play, which satisfies autoplay rules; track swaps before first press only change `src`. Volume slider sets both elements. UI motion stays under 200 ms per tokens; the audio fade is not UI motion. Controls are real buttons with labels, visible focus, and full keyboard use. The bar shows the track label and the active scene title.
123|
124|## Selection and skip override
125|
126|On each active scene change the container runs `selectTrack(sceneEmotion, manifest, currentId)` and stores the result as current. The "Change track" button calls `nextAlternative` and stores that id as the override for the current scene. While the override stands, scene rerenders reuse it without calling `selectTrack`. When the active scene changes, the override clears and selection runs again with the override track passed as `currentTrackId`, so hysteresis compares against what the user last heard. This matches the product rule that a skip holds until the next scene.
127|
128|## Placeholder manifest
129|
130|Choice: static `public/music/manifest.json` fetched by the client, because it needs no route, ships from the CDN, and a later swap replaces files only. `version: 1`, two tracks, `loop: true`, `durationSec: 10`:
131|
132|| Track | File | Label | Emotion source |
133||-------|------|-------|----------------|
134|| oz-test-01 | placeholder/oz-test-01-calma-t01.mp3 | Calm, flute and harp | cluster t01, intensity 0.229, tempo 0.245 |
135|| oz-test-02 | placeholder/oz-test-02-suspenso-t07.mp3 | Suspense, tremolo strings | cluster t07, intensity 0.530, tempo 0.539 |
136|
137|Vectors copy the t01 and t07 centroids rounded to 3 decimals; both already sum to 1.000 at that rounding, and the implementer renormalizes if any edit shifts the sum. `public/music/README.md` covers the swap (replace files and manifest, keep the shape, bump version) plus the CC-BY-NC note for MusicGen output in this non-commercial demo. One test loads the committed manifest through `parseManifest` and asserts every `src` exists under `public/`.
138|
139|## Test list
140|
141|Vitest, beside the code, no DOM library. `core/music.test.ts`: nearest by cosine wins; hysteresis keeps current within margin and switches beyond it; null scene keeps current and returns null without one; empty manifest returns null; `exclude` skips ids; ties follow manifest order; `nextAlternative` cycles all tracks and returns the single track to itself; `parseManifest` accepts the good manifest and rejects each bad shape. `core/reader.test.ts`: reading order, scenes ordered by `n`, every paragraph exactly once, null emotion for failed scenes, no `jev` or `muse_override` fields in output. Manifest test as above. Player and observer logic that can be pure stays pure and tested; the rest is covered by `next build` plus a manual run.
142|
143|## Risks
144|
145|Autoplay: browsers block sound before gesture, so the player must never call play on mount or on track change while `idle`; verify by loading and confirming silence until press. Observer: `find in page` and anchor jumps can set odd scroll positions, so the mount computation plus the keep-last fallback matter more than band tuning. Page weight: the full Oz text ships as server HTML, which is the point of a reader, but keep images and the manifest out of the critical path so first paint stays text. CSP: current `media-src 'self' blob:` and `connect-src 'self'` already cover `/music/` files and the manifest fetch, so no CSP change; note that future remote https track URLs would need a `media-src` edit, and the validator allows them only for that future.
146|
147|## Decisions where the spec was open
148|
149|- Reuse `buildFeatures` from `core/cluster.ts` without moving it: the module imports only types, so it adds nothing unsuitable to the client bundle.
150|- Static manifest over a route: fewer moving parts and the swap stays files only.
151|- Observer band over scroll math: correct on jumps with no cache to maintain.
152|- Two audio elements with volume ramp over Web Audio: no decode code for zero audible gain.
153|- Hysteresis default 0.05: stops flicker between neighboring scenes while real mood shifts still switch.
154|- Server-rendered text with slim client props: full text reaches the reader once, without doubling in the client payload.

3|# Ponytail
4|
5|You are a lazy senior developer. The best code is the code never written. You solve the whole problem with the least new code. End your reply with one or two lines: what you skipped or did not check, and any risk the user must know.
6|

9|## Before you write
10|
11|Read the task and the code it touches. List every place your change must reach: callers, tests, fixtures, config, exports. Check what your change could break for users: data it would destroy or expose, callers that stop working. That is scope. Extra features are not.
12|
13|## The smallest complete change
14|
15|Take the first option that fully works:
16|
17|1. Does it need to exist? Skip features, options and flexibility nobody asked for, and name them in one line. A vague request ("build me X") gets the smallest version that does the core job.
18|2. Already in this codebase (a helper, component, service, pattern)? Use it the way the surrounding code does.
19|3. Standard library or a platform feature? Use it, unless the project has its own. A house component beats a native widget.

24|- Be lazy about the solution, never about the change itself: finish every part the task needs, including the callers, tests and fixtures your change breaks.

1|# Design: task 5 contracts and scene reader
2|
3|Goal: define module contracts so music generation never blocks the reader, then build the scene reader with two placeholder tracks. Real tracks drop in later by replacing files only. Branch `contracts-reader`. Binding inputs: AGENTS.md, SECURITY.md, `core/types.ts`, `core/cluster.ts`, `next.config.ts`, `data/books/oz/music-clusters.json`. This step writes only this doc. The implementer writes `docs/contracts.md`, `core/music.ts`, the manifest, the reader, and the tests.
4|
5|## Module layout
6|
7|```text
8|core/
9|  types.ts    existing book, scene, emotion shapes plus new contract types
10|  music.ts    MusicManifest, Track, parseManifest, selectTrack, nextAlternative
11|  reader.ts   ReaderModel, buildReaderModel
12|  cluster.ts  unchanged, lends buildFeatures to music.ts
13|server/
14|  books.ts    server-only loader: reads oz json, returns Book plus scenes
15|app/
16|  page.tsx    server component: loads data, builds model, renders text
17|  reader.tsx  client container: observer, selection, override, manifest fetch
18|  player/     client player: audio elements, controls, crossfade
19|  tokens.css  unchanged unless a player style needs a token
20|public/music/
21|  manifest.json   placeholder manifest, version 1
22|  README.md       swap guide plus CC-BY-NC note
23|  placeholder/    two mp3 clips, already present
24|```
25|
26|Ownership: `core` is pure and owns every shared type plus selection and model building. `server` owns file reads and env. `app` owns rendering and playback. Import direction is `core <- server` and `core <- app`. Neither `server` nor client components import each other. `app/page.tsx` may import `server/books.ts`. Client files never do.
27|
28|## Core types and signatures
29|
30|New file `core/music.ts`. It reuses `Vector8`, `EMOTIONS`, `FEATURE_WEIGHTS`, and `buildFeatures` from `core/types.ts` and `core/cluster.ts`. Choice: reuse `buildFeatures` in place because `cluster.ts` imports only types, so client code gains no Node or heavy code.
31|
32|```ts
33|export interface Track {
34|  id: string; src: string; label: string;
35|  vector: Vector8; intensity: number; tempo: number;
36|  durationSec: number; loop: boolean;
37|}
38|export interface MusicManifest { version: number; tracks: Track[]; }
39|export function parseManifest(json: unknown): MusicManifest;
40|export function selectTrack(
41|  scene: { vector: Vector8; intensity: number; tempo: number } | null,
42|  manifest: MusicManifest,
43|  currentTrackId?: string | null,
44|  opts?: { margin?: number; exclude?: string[] },
45|): Track | null;
46|export function nextAlternative(
47|  scene: { vector: Vector8; intensity: number; tempo: number } | null,
48|  manifest: MusicManifest,
49|  currentTrackId: string | null,
50|): Track | null;
51|```
52|
53|Rules from the spec: `parseManifest` throws on unknown version, missing fields, a vector not over the 8 ids, numbers outside 0..1, or a `src` that is not a `/music/` relative path or https URL. `selectTrack` scores cosine similarity over `buildFeatures` output, keeps the current track unless the best beats it by `margin` (default 0.05), returns null for a null scene with no current track, returns null for an empty manifest, and breaks ties by manifest order. `nextAlternative` ranks by similarity after the current track and wraps around, so repeats cycle all tracks; one track returns itself. When `scene` is null it ranks on the current track first, which keeps playback stable through failed scenes.
54|
55|Contract-only types live in `core/types.ts`, with no routes and no implementations:
56|
57|```ts
58|export interface ImageRequest { bookId: string; textVersion: string; firstN: number; lastN: number; }
59|export interface ImageResponse { url: string; }
60|export interface ChatRequest { bookId: string; textVersion: string; positionN: number; spoilerMode: boolean; messages: { role: "user" | "assistant"; text: string }[]; }
61|```
62|
63|Quota and budget stay server-only: integer micro-dollars, Redis `INCRBY` reserve before each model call, `DECRBY` refund after. Clients never see keys or raw errors. Image cache key is `firstN..lastN` plus `textVersion` plus `promptVersion` at a deterministic Blob path checked with `head()`; routes return URLs, never bytes.
64|
65|## Reader model shape
66|
67|New pure function in `core/reader.ts`:
68|
69|```ts
70|export interface ReaderParagraph { id: string; n: number; text: string; }
71|export interface ReaderScene {
72|  id: string; title: string;
73|  emotion: { vector: Vector8; intensity: number; tempo: number } | null;
74|  paragraphs: ReaderParagraph[];
75|}
76|export interface ReaderChapter { ch: number; title: string; scenes: ReaderScene[]; }
77|export interface ReaderModel {
78|  bookId: string; textVersion: string; title: string; author: string;
79|  chapters: ReaderChapter[];
80|}
81|export function buildReaderModel(
82|  book: Pick<Book, "id" | "title" | "author" | "chapters" | "paragraphs" | "textVersion">,
83|  analysis: { scenes: AnalyzedScene[] },
84|): ReaderModel;
85|```
86|
87|It joins paragraphs to scenes by `n` ranges in reading order, keeps `final` emotion or null for failed scenes, and drops analysis internals (`jev`, `muse_override`, provenance) so they never reach the client. It throws on unordered scenes or on paragraphs covered zero or two times, reusing the checks in `core/scenes.ts` where they fit.
88|
89|## Server side
90|
91|`server/books.ts` starts with `import 'server-only'` and exposes one function:
92|
93|```ts
94|export function loadOzBook(): { book: Book; scenes: AnalyzedScene[] };
95|```
96|
97|It reads `data/books/oz/book.json`, `scenes.json`, and `analysis.json` with a static import (build time, no request cost) and returns typed values. `app/page.tsx` calls it, runs `buildReaderModel`, and renders chapters, scene sections, and paragraphs as server HTML. Paragraph ids reuse `paragraphId` from `core/ids.ts`, which yields `c12p34` style ids. Choice: text renders on the server and only scene ids plus emotion triples pass as props to client components, so the full book text never duplicates in the client payload.
98|
99|## App side
100|
101|`app/page.tsx` owns layout: centered book column at the reading measure, quiet side panel with the "Chat comes later." placeholder, and the player bar slot. No chat code. Scene sections carry `data-scene-id` with a subtle divider and no other chrome.
102|
103|`app/reader.tsx` is the client container. It owns the manifest fetch (once, from `/music/manifest.json`, parsed with `parseManifest`), the active scene id, the current track id, and the skip override. On manifest failure the reader still renders and the bar shows a short neutral message. It passes the chosen track to the player.
104|
105|`app/player/` owns only playback: audio elements, play state, volume, and the skip button wired through an `onSkip` prop from the container.
106|
107|## Active scene tracking
108|
109|One `IntersectionObserver` watches scene sections. The reading line sits near the top third of the viewport, set with a `rootMargin` band around minus 30 percent. The active scene is the intersecting section whose top edge is nearest above the line. Choice: observer with a band instead of scroll math because jumps and fast scrolls then resolve in one callback with no position cache to maintain. Edge handling: short scenes still cross the band since sections span their paragraphs; when nothing intersects (fast fling between frames), keep the last active scene rather than guessing. On mount, compute from current scroll position so reloads mid book start on the right scene.
110|
111|## Player state machine
112|
113|States: `idle`, `playing`, `paused`, `crossfading`, `no music`. `idle` means no user gesture yet; `no music` means the manifest failed or is empty.
114|
115|```text
116|idle --press play--> playing (or crossfading when a track is already selected)
117|playing --track change--> crossfading --1.5s--> playing
118|playing --press pause--> paused --press play--> playing
119|any --manifest failure or empty--> no music
120|```
121|
122|Two `audio` elements fade against each other on change over about 1.5 s, then the old one pauses. `prefers-reduced-motion` sets the fade to 0. Choice: plain audio elements with a volume ramp instead of Web Audio because nothing here needs decoding or filtering, and native elements keep codec and loop behavior free. Loop is on. Audio starts only after the user presses play, which satisfies autoplay rules; track swaps before first press only change `src`. Volume slider sets both elements. UI motion stays under 200 ms per tokens; the audio fade is not UI motion. Controls are real buttons with labels, visible focus, and full keyboard use. The bar shows the track label and the active scene title.
123|
124|## Selection and skip override
125|
126|On each active scene change the container runs `selectTrack(sceneEmotion, manifest, currentId)` and stores the result as current. The "Change track" button calls `nextAlternative` and stores that id as the override for the current scene. While the override stands, scene rerenders reuse it without calling `selectTrack`. When the active scene changes, the override clears and selection runs again with the override track passed as `currentTrackId`, so hysteresis compares against what the user last heard. This matches the product rule that a skip holds until the next scene.
127|
128|## Placeholder manifest
129|
130|Choice: static `public/music/manifest.json` fetched by the client, because it needs no route, ships from the CDN, and a later swap replaces files only. `version: 1`, two tracks, `loop: true`, `durationSec: 10`:
131|
132|| Track | File | Label | Emotion source |
133||-------|------|-------|----------------|
134|| oz-test-01 | placeholder/oz-test-01-calma-t01.mp3 | Calm, flute and harp | cluster t01, intensity 0.229, tempo 0.245 |
135|| oz-test-02 | placeholder/oz-test-02-suspenso-t07.mp3 | Suspense, tremolo strings | cluster t07, intensity 0.530, tempo 0.539 |
136|
137|Vectors copy the t01 and t07 centroids rounded to 3 decimals; both already sum to 1.000 at that rounding, and the implementer renormalizes if any edit shifts the sum. `public/music/README.md` covers the swap (replace files and manifest, keep the shape, bump version) plus the CC-BY-NC note for MusicGen output in this non-commercial demo. One test loads the committed manifest through `parseManifest` and asserts every `src` exists under `public/`.
138|
139|## Test list
140|
141|Vitest, beside the code, no DOM library. `core/music.test.ts`: nearest by cosine wins; hysteresis keeps current within margin and switches beyond it; null scene keeps current and returns null without one; empty manifest returns null; `exclude` skips ids; ties follow manifest order; `nextAlternative` cycles all tracks and returns the single track to itself; `parseManifest` accepts the good manifest and rejects each bad shape. `core/reader.test.ts`: reading order, scenes ordered by `n`, every paragraph exactly once, null emotion for failed scenes, no `jev` or `muse_override` fields in output. Manifest test as above. Player and observer logic that can be pure stays pure and tested; the rest is covered by `next build` plus a manual run.
142|
143|## Risks
144|
145|Autoplay: browsers block sound before gesture, so the player must never call play on mount or on track change while `idle`; verify by loading and confirming silence until press. Observer: `find in page` and anchor jumps can set odd scroll positions, so the mount computation plus the keep-last fallback matter more than band tuning. Page weight: the full Oz text ships as server HTML, which is the point of a reader, but keep images and the manifest out of the critical path so first paint stays text. CSP: current `media-src 'self' blob:` and `connect-src 'self'` already cover `/music/` files and the manifest fetch, so no CSP change; note that future remote https track URLs would need a `media-src` edit, and the validator allows them only for that future.
146|
147|## Decisions where the spec was open
148|
149|- Reuse `buildFeatures` from `core/cluster.ts` without moving it: the module imports only types, so it adds nothing unsuitable to the client bundle.
150|- Static manifest over a route: fewer moving parts and the swap stays files only.
151|- Observer band over scroll math: correct on jumps with no cache to maintain.
152|- Two audio elements with volume ramp over Web Audio: no decode code for zero audible gain.
153|- Hysteresis default 0.05: stops flicker between neighboring scenes while real mood shifts still switch.
154|- Server-rendered text with slim client props: full text reaches the reader once, without doubling in the client payload.

7|
8|# TypeScript best practices
9|
10|Apply the **type-system-discipline** principle skill first.
11|
12|| Rule | Summary |
13||------|---------|
14|| Discriminated unions | Model variants with a `kind` literal discriminant so impossible states can't be represented. No optional-field bags. |
15|| Branded types | Brand primitives with `& { readonly __brand: "X" }` so they can't be mixed up. Validate once at the boundary. A brand comes from a verifying type guard (`input is AgentId`), never from `as`. |
16|| Constructive modeling | Build the shape so the illegal value can't be constructed. `[T, ...T[]]` for non-empty, `[T, T][]` for even length, `start` plus `duration` for a range. Not a runtime guard, not a wish for refinement types. |
17|| Simplest total type | Keep `T[]` while every operation on it stays total. Strengthen to `NonEmpty<T>` only where the loose type forces `!`, a cast, or a "should never happen" throw. |
18|| `unknown` over `any` | External data is `unknown`. |
19|| Schemas before guards | Before hand-writing a property-by-property type guard, use the repository's runtime schema library and infer the type from the schema, such as `z.infer`. |
20|| No `as` casts | Every `as` is a runtime crash waiting. Cast only after validation. |
21|| Narrowing hierarchy | Discriminant switch > `in` operator > `typeof`/`instanceof` > user-defined type guard > `as`. |
22|| Type guards | Must verify the claim. A lying guard is worse than `as` because the bug hides behind a name that says it's safe. Name them `isX` or `hasX`. |
23|| Exhaustiveness | Inline `const _exhaustive: never = x;` in default arms so the compiler errors when a new variant is added. |
24|| `satisfies` over `as` | Validates the value without widening literal types. |
25|| Boundary validation | Parse where data crosses in, into a named domain type. `Record<string, unknown>` (however spelled) stops at that parse. Trust types inside. See the **boundary-discipline** principle skill. |
26|| Schema-derived types | Reach for `Pick`/`Omit`/`Parameters`/`ReturnType`/`Awaited`/`typeof` before declaring a new interface. |
27|| Object args | Pass objects, not positional, so argument order is self-documenting. Skip on hot paths (per-frame render, tokenizers, parsers). |
28|| Real tests | Don't mock what you can run. Prefer the framework's real test primitives with leak/disposable checks, and verify UI in a running build. Mock only what you can't run locally. |
29|| Structured telemetry | Prefer structured logger diagnostics with enough context to debug from an id. No `console.log` in shipped code. |

13|Rule numbers are stable ids that other skills cite. A removed rule leaves a gap.

15|### Content
16|
17|3. **Superficial -ing phrases.** "highlighting...", "ensuring...", "reflecting...", "showcasing...", "fostering...". Delete or expand with real sources.
18|5. **Vague attributions.** "Experts believe", "Industry reports suggest", "Some critics argue". Name the source or delete.
19|
20|### Language
21|

24|9. **"Not just X, but Y."** State the point directly instead.
25|10. **Rule of three.** Don't force ideas into groups of three. Use the natural number.
26|11. **Synonym cycling.** Protagonist, main character, central figure, hero all in one paragraph. Pick one, repeat it.
27|12. **False ranges.** "from X to Y" where X and Y aren't on a meaningful scale. List topics directly.
28|
29|### Style
30|
31|13. **Em dash overuse.** Avoid em dashes entirely. Use periods or commas only (no parentheses, no en dashes, no hyphen-as-dash substitutes). If a thought needs separation, end the sentence or use a comma.
32|14. **Colon overuse.** Colons are fine before a list or example, not as mid-sentence connectors. 33|15. **Boldface overuse.** Don't bold every proper noun or acronym.

35|17. **Title case headings.** Use sentence case.
36|18. **Decorative emojis.** Remove from headings and bullets.
37|19. **Curly quotes.** Use straight quotes.
38|

40|
41|20. **Chatbot phrases.** "I hope this helps!", "Let me know if...", "Of course!", "Certainly!", "Found the smoking gun!" Remove.

43|

45|
46|23. **Filler phrases.** "In order to" becomes "To". "Due to the fact that" becomes "Because". Delete "It is important to note that".
47|24. **Excessive hedging.** "could potentially possibly be argued that it might" becomes "may".
48|25. **Generic conclusions.** "The future looks bright." State specific plans or facts.
49|
50|### Jargon
51|
52|26. **Abstract metaphor nouns.** Substrate (base), wedge, wedge in (add), vector (way, method), locus, vantage, nexus, primitive as a noun, harness as a metaphor, surface as in "API surface", bedrock, scaffolding as a metaphor, modality, paradigm, gold-plating (more than the job needs), ratchet as a metaphor (the mechanism's real name, or a limit that only tightens), evacuate for moving code (move out), endgame (the last phase), north star, flywheel. 53|
54|### Plain speech
55|
56|27. **Say what it does, not how it feels.** "the database stays close at hand", "SQL you can read", "types that follow your schema" name a feeling. The fix names the mechanism or a number: "`.toSQL()` returns the exact string sent to the database", "a column rename fails the build". 57|28. **Shorten or split dense sentences.** If the reader has to backtrack to parse a sentence, break it in two or drop clauses. One idea per sentence.
58|29. **Active voice.** Prefer it. 61|32. **Mannered prose.** Metaphor or flourish where a literal phrase exists: aphorisms ("wire it or delete it"), rhetorical fragments for effect, personified code ("the plan holds it"), figurative verbs ("rides along", "stands on"), stock framing phrases. "A dial worth turning" becomes "a parameter worth varying". Say what you mean. Rule 26 covers the metaphor nouns.
62|33. **Over-compression.** Dropped articles, verbless fragments, symbol-speak, and abbreviations that make the reader decode instead of read. "Parser rejects bad date → exit 2, no write" becomes "The parser rejects a bad date, exits with code 2, and writes nothing." 32|
33|Design it twice. Require at least two structurally distinct candidates before synthesis, even when the first looks sufficient. This is the **exhaust-the-design-space** principle skill made concrete. Whole-shape alternatives, not point fixes inside one shape.
34|
35|Screen every candidate against [`references/design-red-flags.md`](references/design-red-flags.md) before synthesis. Prefer the design where a change that looks right from one file is right for the whole repo.

42|
43|Default: proceed directly to implementation with the synthesized design. No human checkpoint.

Planned and scoped breakage during fill-in is fine, per the **outcome-oriented-execution** principle skill. For adversarial pressure on the design before implementing, run the **interrogate** skill on the synthesized sketch.
48|

50|

52|
53|Replace `not implemented` bodies with code, pseudocode with logic. The synthesized sketch is the contract. Deviations from it are signal to surface, not friction to absorb silently. - [core/music.ts](/workspace/wt-contracts/core/music.ts): `Track`, `MusicManifest`, `parseManifest`, `selectTrack`, `nextAlternative`.
- [core/reader.ts](/workspace/wt-contracts/core/reader.ts): `ReaderModel`, `buildReaderModel`.
- [core/types.ts](/workspace/wt-contracts/core/types.ts): added `ImageRequest`, `ImageResponse`, `ChatMessage`, `ChatRequest`.
- [server/books.ts](/workspace/wt-contracts/server/books.ts): build-time Oz loader (`server-only`).
- [app/page.tsx](/workspace/wt-contracts/app/page.tsx): static server component rendering the full Oz text.
- [app/reader.tsx](/workspace/wt-contracts/app/reader.tsx): client container (observer, selection, override, manifest fetch).
- [app/active-scene.ts](/workspace/wt-contracts/app/active-scene.ts): pure scene-pick helper.
- [app/player.tsx](/workspace/wt-contracts/app/player.tsx): two-element crossfade player.
- [app/globals.css](/workspace/wt-contracts/app/globals.css): scene divider, sticky player bar, token-only styles.
- [public/music/manifest.json](/workspace/wt-contracts/public/music/manifest.json) and [public/music/README.md](/workspace/wt-contracts/public/music/README.md): two placeholder tracks, swap guide, CC-BY-NC note.
- [docs/contracts.md](/workspace/wt-contracts/docs/contracts.md): module contracts, under 5000 tokens.
- [BUILT_DURING_HACKATHON.md](/workspace/wt-contracts/BUILT_DURING_HACKATHON.md): 2026-10-27 row for task 5.
- Tests: [core/music.test.ts](/workspace/wt-contracts/core/music.test.ts), [core/reader.test.ts](/workspace/wt-contracts/core/reader.test.ts), [core/music-manifest.test.ts](/workspace/wt-contracts/core/music-manifest.test.ts), [app/active-scene.test.ts](/workspace/wt-contracts/app/active-scene.test.ts).

Contracts, one line each

- BookData: `book.json`/`scenes.json`/`analysis.json` feed `buildReaderModel`; reader consumes ids, ranges, titles, and `final` emotion only.
- MusicLibrary: static `public/music/manifest.json` fetched from `/music/manifest.json`; swap means replace files and bump version.
- Track selection: `selectTrack` scores cosine similarity over `buildFeatures`, hysteresis margin 0.05, null scene holds current, ties follow manifest order.
- Player: takes a track or null, owns audio elements, 1.5 s crossfade, loop, play/pause, volume; silent until the user presses play.
- Image API: `{ bookId, textVersion, firstN, lastN }` in, `{ url }` Blob URL out; key is range plus versions at a deterministic path checked with `head()`.
- Chat API: `{ bookId, textVersion, positionN, spoilerMode, messages }` in, streamed text out; context is book text up to `positionN`, prefix first, question last.
- Quotas: server-only integer micro-dollars, `INCRBY` reserve before each call, `DECRBY` refund after; clients see neither keys nor raw errors.

- `npm test`: 14 files, 63 tests, all pass.
- `npm run typecheck`: clean (`next-env.d.ts` present, no typegen needed).
- `npm run build`: prerendered `/` as static, no errors.

- `npm run check:size`: pass, no output.
- `node scripts/check-secrets.mjs --all`: pass.
